title: Retail Sales Performance Report: 2023–2024
executive_summary: Across 520 orders, the business generated $445,325 in total revenue over 2023–2024, with a healthy 10.1% year-over-year increase from 2023 to 2024. The East region led all regions in revenue. Within 2024, revenue accelerated through Q3 before a modest Q4 dip. High-discount Electronics orders represent a notable revenue concentration risk, and a single customer accounts for 6.2% of total revenue.

key_findings.statement: The business recorded 520 orders totalling $445,325 in revenue, yielding an average order value of $856.39.
East led all regions with $130,517 in revenue, followed by North ($124,846), West ($99,428), and South ($90,534). East outpaced South by approximately $40,000.
2024 quarterly revenue rose sharply from $36,108 in Q1 to a peak of $71,675 in Q3, before easing slightly to $68,949 in Q4. Q2 came in at $56,617, ranking third.
Total revenue grew from $211,976 in 2023 to $233,349 in 2024, a year-over-year increase of 10.1%.
22 Electronics orders carried a discount of 20% or more, generating $50,035 in combined revenue — roughly 11.2% of total revenue.

Order revenue is highly right-skewed: the mean is $856.39 but the median is only $313.28, with a standard deviation of $1,295.74. Values range from $5.27 to $7,844.02, indicating a long tail of high-value orders.
Across 222 distinct customers, the top customer alone contributed $27,793 — 6.2% of total revenue — indicating moderate customer concentration.

limitations: The dataset covers only two calendar years (2023–2024); longer historical context would improve trend reliability.
Customer identifiers are anonymised, preventing deeper behavioural or demographic segmentation.
Discount percentages are taken at face value from the export; any upstream data-entry errors would affect the high-discount Electronics filter.
Revenue figures reflect order-level totals and do not account for returns, cancellations, or fulfilment costs.
Regional classification is based on the 'region' field in the raw export; any mis-labelling would distort the regional comparison.
conclusion: The business delivered solid growth in 2023–2024, with a 10.1% revenue increase and a strong Q3 2024 peak. The East and North regions are the primary revenue drivers. The wide gap between mean and median order values highlights a skewed order mix that warrants attention in pricing strategy. The concentration of 6.2% of revenue in a single customer and the $50,035 tied to heavily discounted Electronics orders are areas management should monitor for margin and retention risk.
